newsitem.title: CHINA: China leader praises army before 70th birthday.
newsitem.headline: China leader praises army before 70th birthday.

text.p: Chinese President Jiang Zemin on Thursday praised the People's Liberation Army on the eve of its 70th birthday, and urged the military to rally around the ruling Communist Party before a crucial meeting later this year.

"The People's Liberation Army is a great army because it has always upheld the absolute leadership of the party," said Jiang, who also holds the posts of chairman of the powerful Central Military Commission and Communist Party chief.
Jiang was speaking to a mostly military audience gathered in Beijing's cavernous Great Hall of the People to mark the 70th anniversary of the August 1 founding of the People's Liberation Army (PLA).

Standing under a huge banner that read, "Unite around Comrade Jiang Zemin as the core of the party centre", Jiang urged the military to rally behind the party in the run-up to the party congress later this year that will elect the central committee to run China into the 21st century.

Jiang has been manoeuvring to install himself as the undisputed leader of the party since the death of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping last February, and analysts say the backing of the army is essential to shoring up his position.
"Our party will soon convene its 15th Congress to make major comprehensive, strategic arrangements for national reform, development, stability and other major questions," Jiang said.

"We should tightly unify under Deng Xiaoping's theory of building socialism with Chinese characteristics and the basic line of the party," he said, referring to Deng's market-oriented reforms that have given the military unprecedented opportunities to modernise and to make money in recent years.
Deng had handpicked Jiang as his successor, and Jiang has vowing repeatedly to carry on the sweeping economic reforms launched by his mentor.

Diplomats said the most prominent victim of the coming party reshuffle would be top army general and Politburo standing committee member Liu Huaqing, whom Jiang wants to replace with Defence Minister Chi Haotian or military commission vice-chairman Zhang Wannian.
"The full expectation is that Liu Huaqing will be on his way out at the party congress and that Zhang Wannian or Chi Haotian will take his place," one Western diplomat said.
Nonetheless, General Liu, who presided over Thursday's rally, praised Jiang's speech and told soldiers and officers to implement the spirit of Jiang's words and to avoid factionalism.
"We should more tightly unite around Jiang Zemin, be of one heart and one mind, and struggle to build the army into a powerful and modern army," Liu said.

While Jiang never served in the army and lacks the military credentials of Deng and Chairman Mao Zedong, he has won the support of the military partly because there was no clear alternative to his leadership, diplomats said.
"The PLA's main interest is not power broking, it is stability, and they will back whoever can provide that," the diplomat said.
Jiang also played up the army's role in China's breakneck economic growth, saying territorial integrity and internal stability were essential for development.
"We should struggle hard to build the army into a powerful, modern, standardised and revolutionary army," Jiang said.
Behind the scenes, Jiang has moved boldly to assert his authority, issuing an internal directive this month citing a wave of crime and corruption in the army and ordering rectification.
"Jiang Zemin has played the army very, very well," the diplomat said. "He has shown his acute political skills."
